# A program's top level is its body. Visual nodes written outside any component
# or window are what the program renders, with the package's own vars as the
# state they read -- so `component main` is a wrapper a program no longer has to
# write (#135).
#
# passRootWindow turns that body into the window the program opens at, before
# any other pass runs. That is the whole implementation strategy: two dozen
# lowering passes and five platforms already walk pkg.Windows, and a second
# shape carrying a body is a second thing each of them has to know -- which is
# exactly where #133 came from. So the assertions below are equalities: the
# top-level form must generate what the same program written as a window
# generates, on every target.

sngl generate --platform=html --lang=none --out=t-html top.sngl
sngl generate --platform=html --lang=none --out=w-html win.sngl
cmpgen t-html/index.html w-html/index.html

sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --out=t-bt top.sngl
sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --out=w-bt win.sngl
cmpgen t-bt/model.go w-bt/model.go

sngl generate --platform=fyne --lang=go --out=t-fy top.sngl
sngl generate --platform=fyne --lang=go --out=w-fy win.sngl
cmpgen t-fy/model.go w-fy/model.go

sngl generate --platform=android --lang=kotlin --out=t-an top.sngl
sngl generate --platform=android --lang=kotlin --out=w-an win.sngl
cmpgen t-an/MainScreen.kt w-an/MainScreen.kt

# The state is the package's, and it has to reach the page as state rather than
# as a name nothing declared -- the failure mode #133 documented.
grep 'var state = \{ n: 0 \}' t-html/index.html
grep 'state.n = state.n \+ 1' t-html/index.html

# A body and declared windows coexist: the body is the root the program opens
# at, the windows are what it navigates to. The root takes index.html even
# though it is not the only window, which is what distinguishes "first" from
# "only".
sngl generate --platform=html --lang=none --out=both both.sngl
exists both/index.html
exists both/about/index.html
grep 'visits' both/index.html
grep 'About this app' both/about/index.html

# A component instantiated with no block parses as a call statement, not a
# visual node -- `counter()` is an *ast.CallStmt. It is the same package body,
# and it is the shape a top-level program usually has: composition at the top,
# behaviour in components (which is also what a test names, since a composition
# root has no instance to hand a test).
# The instance's state is renamed per instance by the inliner, which is what a
# component instantiated in a body has always done -- it is the composition
# that is new here, not the inlining.
sngl generate --platform=html --lang=none --out=comp compose.sngl
grep 'var state = \{ n__inst0: 0 \}' comp/index.html
grep 'state.n__inst0 = state.n__inst0 \+ 1' comp/index.html

-- top.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

var n = 0

vbox {
    text(value="{n}")
    button #inc(text="+", @click { n = n + 1 })
}

-- win.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:app"

var n = 0

window {
    vbox {
        text(value="{n}")
        button #inc(text="+", @click { n = n + 1 })
    }
}

-- both.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:app"

var visits = 0

vbox {
    text(value="visits: {visits}")
    link(href="/about", text="About")
}

window #about(title="About", href="/about") {
    vbox {
        text(value="About this app")
        link(href="/", text="Home")
    }
}

-- compose.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

counter()

component counter {
    var n = 0
    vbox {
        text(value="{n}")
        button #inc(text="+", @click { n = n + 1 })
    }
}
